title: Finite exact-couple boundaries as initial g-images of iterated alpha kernels
statement: Let $C$ be an abelian category and $X$ a type-zero bigraded exact couple [def-sp-exact-couple]. Write $T$ for its canonical cycle-boundary tower, $\alpha^r_{p,q}:D^{p,q}\to D^{p-r,q+r}$ for its outgoing alpha iterate, and $g_{p,q}:D^{p,q}\to E^{p,q}$ for its transported initial g [def-sp-convergence]. For every $r\in\mathbb N$ and $p,q\in\mathbb Z$, $T.B_r(p,q)=g_{p,q}(\ker\alpha^r_{p,q})$ as subobjects of $E^{p,q}$. No diagonal cocone or tail assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 011T, finite boundary formula; Tag 0AMJ, shifted exact-couple boundary formula

proof.text: Use pageCouple_image_prefix to obtain the iterated mono inclusions I and incoming alpha powers A. Induction on the recurrence identifies A with incomingAlphaIter. The outgoing alpha iterate has the same image as its incoming form at (p-r,q+r), so its image is the image of the mono I_r there. The canonical isomorphism of these image domains, composed with the image epimorphism of alphaIter r, gives an epi e with e followed by I_r equal to alphaIter r. Alpha compatibility and the appended-alpha recurrence identify the kernel of e followed by page alpha with the kernel of alphaIter(r+1). Monicity of I_r likewise identifies ker e with ker alphaIter r.

The finite cycle formula shows that initialG factors through Z_r, since initialG followed by original f is zero. Let c be this unique factorization. Apply finiteCycle_derived_comparison to obtain c followed by the cycle projection equal to e followed by the transported page g. Exact_alpha and epimorphic image factorization identify image(dInto) with the direct image under transported page g of the kernel of page alpha. Reindex all endpoint transports by integer arithmetic.

Prove the boundary equality by induction on r. At zero alphaIter is an isomorphism and both sides are bottom. For the successor use the epi e and lift c of the previous steps. The inductive boundary formula and the kernel of the cycle projection imply ker(projection) is contained in c(ker(e followed by page alpha)). To identify the pullback of g(ker(page alpha)) with this c image, lift a generalized element through the image epi and then through e, after epimorphic refinements. Its lifted representative is killed by e followed by page alpha. Subtract its c image; the difference is killed by projection, hence belongs to the displayed c image by the kernel containment. Add back the representative. Factorization descends along the composite epimorphic refinement by cancellation against the cokernel of the subobject inclusion. Conversely the kernel condition immediately gives the pullback factorization. Apply the tower successor boundary recurrence, compose image functors, and substitute the alphaIter(r+1) kernel equality.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteBoundary_alphaKernel
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C]
    (X : BigradedExactCouple C 0) (r : ℕ) (p q : ℤ) :
    X.cycleBoundaryTower.B r p q =
      (Subobject.«exists» (X.initialG p q)).obj (kernelSubobject (X.alphaIter r p q))
